output.reply: Nvidia's data-center segment, which sells accelerators and systems to cloud companies, was the large majority of its revenue last quarter, so the AI link carries real weight for the company. The strongest point against is that its largest customers also design their own AI chips. I propose a wrong-if tied to that customer concentration, and a positional time frame.

findings.fact: Nvidia said its data-center segment, which sells accelerators and systems to cloud companies, was the large majority of its revenue last quarter. The exact share was not stated in the source.
Nvidia named the big cloud companies as its largest customers, so its AI revenue depends on a small group of buyers.
Several of the largest cloud companies design their own AI chips and use them alongside the accelerators they buy.
The largest cloud companies said they plan to keep raising AI data-center spending next year.

The customers that fund Nvidia's AI demand are also building their own chips, so the same buyers could both raise and cap Nvidia's share of their spending. This is an inference from the findings above.

why.shared: Nvidia earns most of its revenue from accelerators sold into AI data centers, as its own results show

reasons.text: Data-center accelerators and systems were the large majority of last quarter's revenue, and big cloud buyers plan to raise AI spending next year.

against.text: Its largest customers also design their own AI chips and use them alongside Nvidia's, which could limit how much of their spending it keeps.

wrongIfOptions.text: the big cloud companies shift more of their AI workloads onto chips they design themselves, away from Nvidia accelerators
the largest cloud companies cut or pause their AI data-center spending plans
data-center accelerators stop being the large majority of Nvidia's revenue

timeFramePick.reason: The why rests on spending plans for next year and customer chip choices that play out over a few months.

pick.value: the big cloud companies shift more of their AI workloads onto chips they design themselves, away from Nvidia accelerators
pick.reason: It is the strongest point against and goes straight at Nvidia's customer base.
